tasks.title: Create Project Structure and Type Definitions
tasks.description: Establish the foundational project structure with proper TypeScript types and interfaces for the roguelike game
tasks.details: Create a well-organized file structure: /src/types/index.ts for all game types (GamePhase, Character, Enemy, ShopItem, etc.), /src/utils/ for utility functions, /src/components/ for UI components, /src/hooks/ for custom React hooks. Define core interfaces: GameState, Character (with stats like Ferocity, Quickness, Survival, Instinct), Enemy, ShopItem, LabUpgrade. Use TypeScript 5.0+ features like const assertions and satisfies operator for better type safety. Implement proper enum definitions for phases: 'combat' | 'shop' | 'death' | 'lab'.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify all types compile without errors, ensure proper IntelliSense support, validate type definitions cover all game entities mentioned in PRD

tasks.title: Implement Core Game State Management
tasks.description: Create a centralized state management system using React Context and useReducer for game state
tasks.details: Use React 18's useReducer with TypeScript for state management. Create GameContext with actions: SET_PHASE, UPDATE_CHARACTERS, ADD_ENEMY, RESET_COMBAT, etc. Implement state persistence using localStorage for development. Consider using Immer (v10.0+) for immutable state updates as mentioned in PRD for future scalability: `import { produce } from 'immer'`. Structure: GameProvider component wrapping the app, custom hooks like useGameState(), useGameActions(). Initial state should include: currentPhase, playerTeam, enemies, shopItems, labUpgrades, runStats.
tasks.testStrategy: Test state transitions between phases, verify state persistence, ensure all actions properly update state without mutations

tasks.title: Build Phase Tracker Component
tasks.description: Create a persistent left-side phase tracker that displays current game phase and overall progress
tasks.details: Build a fixed-position sidebar using Tailwind CSS with classes: `fixed left-0 top-0 h-full w-64 bg-gray-800 text-white p-4`. Display current phase with visual indicators (icons, progress bars). Use React icons (react-icons v4.12+) for phase icons: FaSword (combat), FaStore (shop), FaSkull (death), FaFlask (lab). Include phase history/progress visualization. Implement smooth transitions with Tailwind's transition classes. Make responsive with `hidden md:block` for mobile.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify tracker remains visible across all phases, test responsive behavior, validate phase transitions update tracker correctly

tasks.title: Create Main Layout Container with Overlay System
tasks.description: Implement the main app layout that supports phase screens and overlay UI elements
tasks.details: Create a flexible layout system using CSS Grid or Flexbox: `grid-cols-[256px_1fr]` for sidebar + main content. Implement overlay system using React Portals and z-index management. Main container should handle: phase tracker (left), main content area (center), floating overlays (notifications, modals). Use Tailwind's layer utilities: `relative z-10` for overlays. Implement OverlayProvider context for managing multiple overlays. Support for future UI elements like player info panels, notifications without modifying phase screens.
tasks.testStrategy: Test layout responsiveness, verify overlays render correctly above content, ensure phase transitions don't break layout

tasks.title: Refactor Existing Combat System

tasks.title: Design and Implement Shop and Lab Item Type System
tasks.description: Create comprehensive type definitions and data structures for Shop and Lab items, including new item categories, effects, upgrades, and progression mechanics to support income, healing, recruitment, and genetic engineering features.
tasks.details: Create /src/types/items.ts with comprehensive item type definitions. Define base ItemType interface with properties: id, name, description, price, rarity, category, effects, requirements. Implement item categories: CONSUMABLE (healing items, buffs), UPGRADE (stat boosters, ability enhancers), FACILITY (income generators, recruitment tools), GENETIC (evolution catalysts, gene modifiers). Create ItemEffect interface supporting multiple effect types: HEAL, STAT_BOOST, INCOME_MODIFIER, RECRUITMENT_BONUS, GENETIC_ENHANCEMENT. Implement item requirement system for progression-based unlocks using RequirementChecker utility. Create item effect application system with EffectProcessor class. Add item persistence support for save/load functionality.
tasks.testStrategy: Create comprehensive unit tests for all item type interfaces and ensure proper TypeScript compilation. Test ItemRegistry correctly manages item definitions and filtering by category/rarity. Verify RequirementChecker properly validates unlock conditions. Test EffectProcessor applies item effects correctly without side effects. Validate item pricing calculations with rarity multipliers. Test item serialization/deserialization for persistence. tasks.title: Refactor CombatScreen into Modular Combat System
tasks.description: Break down the monolithic CombatScreen component into a modular, maintainable combat system with separate UI components and logic modules.
tasks.details:
Decompose the existing CombatScreen into multiple focused components and utilities:

**UI Components Structure:**
- `/src/components/Combat/CombatScreen.tsx` - Main orchestrator component
- `/src/components/Combat/UnitCard.tsx` - Individual unit display with health, stats, abilities
- `/src/components/Combat/HealthBar.tsx` - Reusable health visualization component
- `/src/components/Combat/InitiativeDisplay.tsx` - Turn order and initiative tracking
- `/src/components/Combat/CombatControlPanel.tsx` - Action buttons and combat controls
- `/src/components/Combat/CombatLog.tsx` - Action history and feedback display
- `/src/components/Combat/VictoryOverlay.tsx` - End-of-combat results screen

**Logic Modules:**
- `/src/utils/combat/attackLogic.ts` - Damage calculation, hit resolution, critical hits
- `/src/utils/combat/initiativeManager.ts` - Turn order calculation and management
- `/src/utils/combat/combatState.ts` - State machine for combat phases
- `/src/utils/combat/combatEffects.ts` - Status effects, buffs, debuffs management

**Custom Hooks:**
- `useCombatState()` - Manages overall combat state and phase transitions
- `useInitiative()` - Handles turn order and initiative calculations
- `useCombatActions()` - Manages attack actions and ability usage
- `useHealthManagement()` - Tracks and updates unit health states

**Implementation Approach:**
Use composition over inheritance for component design. Implement proper prop drilling prevention with React Context for combat state. Use TypeScript strict mode with proper interface definitions for all combat entities. Implement error boundaries for robust error handling. Use React.memo for performance optimization on frequently re-rendered components like HealthBar. Ensure all components are pure functions where possible for better testability.

**Maintainability Features:**
- Clear separation of concerns between UI and logic
- Consistent naming conventions and file organization
- Comprehensive TypeScript interfaces for all data structures
- Modular architecture supporting easy feature additions
- Proper abstraction layers for future extensibility
tasks.testStrategy:
**Component Testing:**
- Unit test each component in isolation using React Testing Library
- Test UnitCard renders correctly with various unit states (healthy, damaged, dead)
- Verify HealthBar displays accurate health percentages and animations
- Test InitiativeDisplay shows correct turn order and highlights active unit
- Validate CombatControlPanel enables/disables buttons based on game state

**Logic Module Testing:**
- Test attackLogic.ts with various damage scenarios and edge cases
- Verify initiativeManager.ts correctly calculates and sorts turn order
- Test combatState.ts state machine transitions and invalid state handling
- Validate combatEffects.ts properly applies and removes status effects

**Integration Testing:**
- Test complete combat flow from start to victory/defeat
- Verify proper communication between UI components and logic modules
- Test error handling and recovery scenarios
- Validate performance with multiple units and complex combat scenarios

**Regression Testing:**
- Ensure all existing combat functionality remains intact
- Test Reset button functionality works correctly
- Verify integration with existing game state management
- Validate smooth transitions to Shop and Death phases

tasks.title: Link Attack Bonus Damage to Stats
tasks.description: Implement logic so that attack damage calculations take into account relevant unit stats (e.g., Ferocity, Quickness, etc.), allowing for stat-based scaling of attack power.
tasks.details: Create stat-based damage calculation system in /src/utils/combat.ts. Extend existing damage calculation functions to incorporate unit stats: base damage + (Ferocity * 0.5) + (Quickness * 0.3) for physical attacks. Define stat scaling coefficients in /src/config/statScaling.ts with different multipliers per stat type and attack type. Update DamageCalculation interface to include statModifiers property. Implement calculateStatBonus() function that takes unit stats and returns damage modifier. Modify existing combat functions like executeAttack() to use new stat-based calculations. Add support for different scaling formulas per creature type (Tiger might scale more with Ferocity, Eagle with Quickness). Update type definitions in /src/types/combat.ts to include StatDamageModifier interface. Consider diminishing returns for very high stats using logarithmic scaling: Math.log(1 + stat) * multiplier. Ensure backwards compatibility with existing combat system.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests for stat damage calculations with various stat combinations and verify scaling formulas produce expected results. Test edge cases like zero stats, maximum stats, and negative modifiers. Verify different creature types apply correct stat scaling coefficients. Test combat integration by simulating battles with high-stat vs low-stat units and confirming damage differences. Ensure existing combat functionality remains unaffected and damage calculations are consistent across different attack types.

tasks.title: Link Stats to Characters and Combat Mechanics
tasks.description: Integrate the stat system with character attributes and combat mechanics, ensuring all attacks scale with appropriate stats and core attributes like health and initiative are stat-based.
tasks.details:
Create comprehensive stat-to-mechanic linking system by extending existing type definitions and combat logic:

**Type System Updates:**
- Extend Character interface in /src/types/character.ts to include statModifiers and baseStats properties
- Update CombatUnit interface to reference character stats for health, initiative, and damage calculations
- Create StatScaling interface defining multipliers for each stat-to-mechanic relationship

**Stat-to-Mechanic Mappings:**
- Link max health calculation: baseHealth + (Survival * healthPerSurvival)
- Link initiative calculation: baseInitiative + (Quickness * initiativePerQuickness)  
- Link attack damage: baseDamage + (Ferocity * damagePerFerocity) for physical attacks
- Link speed-based attacks: baseDamage + (Quickness * speedDamageMultiplier)
- Link XP gain: baseXP * (1 + Instinct * xpMultiplier)
- Link ability power: basePower + (Instinct * abilityPowerPerInstinct)

**Implementation Files:**
- Update /src/utils/statCalculations.ts with functions: calculateMaxHealth(), calculateInitiative(), calculateAttackDamage(), calculateXPGain()
- Modify /src/utils/combat.ts to use stat-based calculations instead of hardcoded values
- Update character creation logic in /src/utils/characterGeneration.ts to properly initialize stat-based attributes
- Create /src/config/statScaling.ts with configurable scaling coefficients

**Integration Points:**
- Refactor existing combat damage calculations to use new stat-based system
- Update character leveling logic to recalculate derived stats when base stats change
- Ensure UI components display stat-influenced values correctly
tasks.testStrategy: Create comprehensive unit tests for stat calculation functions with various stat combinations and verify scaling produces expected results. Test edge cases including zero stats, maximum stats, and stat changes during combat. Verify character creation properly initializes all stat-based attributes. Test combat integration ensures attacks use correct stat scaling and health/initiative calculations are accurate. Create integration tests verifying stat changes immediately update derived values like max health and attack damage. Test XP gain scaling with different Instinct values and ability power calculations for various ability types.

tasks.title: Implement Passive and Unit-Specific Abilities System
tasks.description: Create a unified system for defining and managing passive abilities for all units (Tiger, Bear, Eagle, etc.) with trigger-based execution and combat system integration.
tasks.details: Refactor the existing ability system to focus on passive abilities by extending /src/utils/abilities.ts. Create a unified PassiveAbility interface with properties: id, name, description, triggerType (END_TURN, ON_ATTACK, ON_DAMAGE_TAKEN, COMBAT_START, ENEMY_DEFEATED), execute(), and isActive(). Implement PassiveAbilityManager class to handle ability registration, trigger detection, and execution timing. Define unit-specific passive abilities: Tiger (First Strike - bonus damage on first attack each turn), Bear (Thick Hide - damage reduction passive + Intimidate on combat start), Eagle (Keen Eyes - initiative bonus + Aerial Advantage on attack). Create trigger system using event-driven architecture with custom events or observer pattern. Integrate with combat system by adding trigger points in combat flow: before/after attacks, turn transitions, damage calculations. Remove or refactor any existing active ability logic to focus on passive effects. Update ability execution to work with stat system integration for scaling effects. Create /src/types/abilities.ts for comprehensive type definitions including TriggerType enum, PassiveAbility interface, and AbilityEffect types. Add ability testing utilities in /src/utils/abilityTesting.ts for development and debugging.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests for PassiveAbilityManager with mock combat scenarios to verify correct trigger timing and execution. Test each unit's passive abilities individually: verify Tiger's first strike bonus applies only once per turn, confirm Bear's damage reduction calculates correctly, ensure Eagle's initiative buff affects turn order. Test multiple passive abilities on same unit don't conflict or create infinite loops. Verify passive abilities integrate properly with stat-based damage calculations. Create integration tests with combat system to ensure triggers fire at correct combat phases. Test ability persistence across combat rounds and phase transitions. Add manual testing scenarios in game loop to validate passive effects are visible and functional during actual gameplay.
